newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus documentary unit to invest 150 mln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus documentary unit to invest 150 mln Ffr.

text.p: Docstar, the documentary unit of French pay TV station Canal Plus, will invest 150 million francs between now and the year 2000 in building up catalogues, in co-production and distribution of documentaries, Catherine Lamour, documentary director of Canal Plus, said on Monday.
"Docstar aims to become the obligatory partner for those who make animal films," she told a news conference at the MIP television trade fair in Cannes.

"The same goes for subjects related to history, science, discovery and adventure. Docstar could also be interested in social concerns, but only if the theme or the producer guarantees an international audience," she said.
"Our wish today is to increase significantly our investment between now and the year 2000," she said.

Docstar, which buys documentary television or video rights for seven to 15 years and puts up $100,000 to $150,000 per hour for programmes made or broadcast in Europe, expects to invest 20 million francs in 1997, she said.
